c.st: Why do LLM pelicans look like this?
c.x:
Re house - the reason why people (not just kids) will draw the same symbolically looking house is due to the question itself: they want you to recognize the house in what they've drawn. No one wants to fail, everyone wants to please, and it's the same with llms.

If instead you ask to draw some fancy interestingly looking house you'll get more variety - now the task is not to have the question giver recognize the house in their drawing, but to show how they imagine fancy or interesting house.

c.st: Original 1851 reviews of Moby-Dick
c.x: If you're looking for something shorter and more readable about whaling, I'd recommend In the Heart of the Sea. The (nonfiction) story told there was used by Melville as inspiration for Moby Dick. Unlike Moby Dick, that was a book I could not put down, but my brain is also the size of a peanut.

c.st: The Art of Whaling: Illustrations from the Logbooks of Nantucket Whaleships
c.x: I heartily recommend "In The Heart Of The Sea: The Tragedy of the Whaleship Essex" if anyone is interested in learning more about Nantucket whaling. It is a captivating true story that talks about the characters and culture involved in the whaling community.  It is also apparently the story that inspired Melville to write Moby Dick.

c.st: A good measurement culture where numbers don’t replace common sense
c.x:
Having economics degree, I figured this out of evolutionary dynamics theory -- a more sophisticated creature will outplay a less sophisticated (in this case it's an employee with creativity against a manager that just uses KPI).

Later I found out this rule was articulated in mid-XX-century in sociology -- the Goodhart's law: "a metric stops being a good metric as soon as it is used to make decisions".

I love computers and computer graphics, but sometimes a hand-drawn graph just takes the cake.
